tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Describing Dance in Writing

questions.question: Q: What are the four key areas you should cover when describing dance movement?
questions.correctAnswer: Action, dynamics, space and relationships (A D S R). Together, they provide a complete description of what happens, how it happens, where it happens and how dancers interact.

questions.question: Q: Give an example of describing dynamics accurately rather than vaguely.
questions.correctAnswer: Vague: 'The dancer moved nicely.' Accurate: 'The dancer performed a sustained, slow développé with light, flowing quality, gradually extending through the leg and arm.'

questions.question: Q: Why should you avoid subjective language like 'beautiful' in exam answers?
questions.correctAnswer: Subjective language does not describe what actually happens in the dance. Examiners reward precise technical observation — describing dynamics, actions and spatial design — rather than personal opinion.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Describing Dance in Writing

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between unison and canon?
questions.correctAnswer: In unison, dancers perform the same movement at exactly the same time. In canon, dancers perform the same movement but start at different times, creating a ripple or wave effect.

questions.question: Q: How can you show detailed knowledge of a professional work in your written description?
questions.correctAnswer: Reference specific moments, sections or counts — for example, 'In Section 2, the trio performs canon with sharp, percussive arm gestures while travelling in a circular pathway at mid level.'
